events.notificationTitle: The day the UN was born
events.notificationBody: In 1945, the UN Charter took effect and the United Nations began.

sources.name: United Nations - United Nations Day

events.title: Treaties end the Thirty Years' War in Germany
events.summary: The Peace of Westphalia brings the emperor, German princes, France, and Sweden to terms.
events.description: On October 24, 1648, a treaty signed as part of the Peace of Westphalia brought together Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand III, the German princes, France, and Sweden. The settlements of 1648 ended the German phase of the Thirty Years' War.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Peace of Westphalia

events.title: Zambia becomes independent
events.summary: The former Northern Rhodesia becomes a sovereign nation.
events.description: On October 24, 1964, Zambia attained independence. The United States recognized the new nation the same day, raising its consulate at Lusaka to an embassy.

sources.name: U.S. Office of the Historian - Zambia

events.title: A rocket camera takes the first photos of Earth from space
events.summary: Film from a V-2 launched in New Mexico shows Earth from 65 miles up.
events.description: On October 24, 1946, a 35-millimeter motion picture camera aboard a V-2 missile launched from White Sands, New Mexico, captured the first pictures of Earth as seen from space, from an altitude of 65 miles.

sources.name: Smithsonian Air & Space Magazine - The First Photo From Space

events.title: Henry V's army wins at Agincourt
events.summary: An outnumbered English army defeats the French in the Hundred Years' War.
events.description: On October 25, 1415, the English army led by King Henry V defeated a numerically superior French force at Agincourt. The victory made possible England's later conquest of Normandy.
events.notificationTitle: The underdogs of Agincourt
events.notificationBody: In 1415, Henry V's outnumbered army defeated the French at Agincourt.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Battle of Agincourt

events.title: The Charge of the Light Brigade at Balaklava
events.dateNote: October 13 in the Julian calendar then used in Russia.
events.summary: A Crimean War battle inspires Tennyson's famous poem.
events.description: On October 25, 1854, British and Russian forces fought the indecisive Battle of Balaklava during the Crimean War. It is best known for the Charge of the Light Brigade, which inspired Alfred, Lord Tennyson's poem.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Battle of Balaklava

events.title: Lisbon surrenders to Portuguese and crusader forces
events.summary: A months-long siege ends with the city's capture from the Almoravids.
events.description: On October 25, 1147, the gates of Lisbon opened and a siege by Afonso Henriques of Portugal and crusaders bound for the Second Crusade came to an end. The capture of the city from the Almoravids was the only major Christian victory of that crusade.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Siege of Lisbon

events.title: Microsoft launches Windows XP
events.summary: The operating system goes on sale worldwide after a New York launch.
events.description: On October 25, 2001, Microsoft launched Windows XP in New York, making the operating system available on new personal computers and in stores around the world.

sources.name: Microsoft Source - Windows XP Is Here!

events.title: The world's last natural smallpox case is found
events.summary: A case in Somalia marks the end of naturally occurring smallpox.
events.description: On October 26, 1977, the world's last naturally occurring case of smallpox was discovered in the Merca district of Somalia. Two years of active searching followed to make certain transmission had stopped.
events.notificationTitle: The last case of a deadly disease
events.notificationBody: In 1977, the world's last natural smallpox case was found in Somalia.

sources.name: World Health Organization - Statue commemorates smallpox eradication
CDC MMWR - 25th Anniversary of the Last Case of Naturally Acquired Smallpox

events.title: The Football Association is formed in London
events.summary: A meeting at a London tavern creates English football's governing body.
events.description: On October 26, 1863, the Football Association was formed at a meeting at the Freemasons' Tavern in Great Queen Street, London. It became English football's governing body.

sources.name: The Football Association - A history of the FA

events.title: Austria adopts permanent neutrality
events.summary: The Austrian parliament passes a constitutional law on neutrality.
events.description: On October 26, 1955, the Austrian National Council passed the constitutional law establishing Austria's permanent neutral status.

sources.name: CVCE (University of Luxembourg) - Constitutional Law on the Neutrality of Austria

events.title: The Erie Canal is completed
events.summary: A waterway links the Hudson River to the Great Lakes.
events.description: On October 26, 1825, the Erie Canal was finished, two years ahead of schedule. Connecting the Hudson River valley with the Great Lakes, it stimulated migration into central and western New York.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Erie Canal

events.title: New York's first subway line opens
events.summary: The IRT opens a 9.1-mile underground line with 28 stations.
events.description: On October 27, 1904, the Interborough Rapid Transit Company opened New York City's first underground subway line. The 9.1-mile route had 28 stations, running from City Hall to Grand Central, across to Times Square, and up to 145th Street and Broadway.
events.notificationTitle: New York goes underground
events.notificationBody: In 1904, New York City's first subway line opened.

sources.name: Tenement Museum - On This Day: 1904, First Underground Subway

events.title: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines becomes independent
events.summary: The last of the Windward Islands to gain independence.
events.description: On October 27, 1979, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines achieved full independence, becoming the last of the Windward Islands to do so after a referendum earlier that year.

sources.name: U.S. Office of the Historian - Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

events.title: Turkmenistan declares independence
events.summary: The Soviet republic breaks away as the USSR nears collapse.
events.description: On October 27, 1991, Turkmenistan, a constituent republic of the Soviet Union since 1925, declared its independence.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Turkmenistan

events.title: Amsterdam's name appears in writing for the first time
events.summary: A toll privilege from the Count of Holland is the city's oldest document.
events.description: On October 27, 1275, Count Floris V of Holland issued a toll privilege exempting the people living near the dam on the Amstel from tolls in his territory. The document, drawn up in Leiden, is the first to mention Amsterdam by name, and the city celebrates the date as its birthday.

sources.name: Stadsarchief Amsterdam - Tolprivilege
Museum.nl - Tolprivilege uit 1275 (Stadsarchief Amsterdam)

events.title: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated
events.summary: President Grover Cleveland dedicates a monument to French-American friendship.
events.description: On October 28, 1886, President Grover Cleveland dedicated the Statue of Liberty, mounted on its pedestal. Funded by contributions from the French people and designed by sculptor Frederic-Auguste Bartholdi, it commemorates the friendship of the United States and France.
events.notificationTitle: Liberty lifts her torch
events.notificationBody: In 1886, President Grover Cleveland dedicated the Statue of Liberty.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Statue of Liberty

events.title: Czechoslovakia declares independence
events.summary: A new state emerges from the collapsing Austro-Hungarian Empire.
events.description: On October 28, 1918, Tomas Masaryk, Edvard Benes, and other leaders declared an independent Czechoslovak state as Austria-Hungary collapsed at the end of World War I. France and other Allied powers quickly recognized it.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Czechoslovakia

events.title: Greece rejects Mussolini's ultimatum
events.summary: Greece's refusal, marked as Ohi Day, brings it into World War II.
events.description: In the early hours of October 28, 1940, the Italian ambassador handed Greek Prime Minister Ioannis Metaxas an ultimatum from Mussolini demanding that Italian forces be allowed to occupy strategic sites in Greece. Greece rejected it, and the day is commemorated as Ohi Day, the 'Day of No'.

sources.name: Greek News Agenda (Hellenic Secretariat General for Communication) - 28th of October 1940: The Greek Ohi Day

events.title: Constantine wins the Battle of the Milvian Bridge
events.summary: Victory over Maxentius near Rome confirms Constantine as ruler of the West.
events.description: On October 28, 312, Constantine defeated his rival Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge near Rome. The victory confirmed Constantine's role as ruler of the Western Roman Empire.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Battle of Milvian Bridge

events.title: The Republic of Turkey is proclaimed
events.summary: Mustafa Kemal's nationalists establish a republic with Ankara as capital.
events.description: On October 29, 1923, the Turkish republic was proclaimed, with Ankara named as its capital. It followed the abolition of the sultanate in 1922 and the Treaty of Lausanne in July 1923.
events.notificationTitle: A republic is born in Ankara
events.notificationBody: In 1923, the Republic of Turkey was proclaimed.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Kemal Ataturk

events.title: The first message crosses the ARPANET
events.summary: A computer at UCLA reaches one at Stanford, but crashes two letters in.
events.description: On October 29, 1969, a team led by UCLA computer scientist Leonard Kleinrock sent the first message between networked computers at UCLA and the Stanford Research Institute. Graduate student Charley Kline typed the first two letters of 'login' before the network crashed.

sources.name: University of California - Lo and behold: The internet

events.title: John Glenn returns to space at 77
events.summary: The former Mercury astronaut becomes the oldest person to fly in space.
events.description: On October 29, 1998, space shuttle Discovery launched on mission STS-95 with John Glenn aboard. At 77, Glenn became the oldest person to fly in space.

sources.name: NASA - STS-95

events.title: Black Tuesday deepens the 1929 stock market crash
events.summary: Share prices fall nearly 12 percent a day after Black Monday.
events.description: On October 29, 1929, known as Black Tuesday, the New York stock market dropped nearly 12 percent, following a fall of nearly 13 percent the day before. By mid-November the Dow had lost almost half its value.

sources.name: Federal Reserve History - Stock Market Crash of 1929

events.title: Orson Welles broadcasts The War of the Worlds
events.summary: A radio drama about a Martian invasion is mistaken for news by some listeners.
events.description: On October 30, 1938, Orson Welles and his Mercury Theatre on the Air broadcast an adaptation of H.G. Wells's The War of the Worlds as a simulated news bulletin about Martians invading New Jersey. Although it was announced as a dramatization, some listeners who tuned in late took it for real news.
events.notificationTitle: The night Martians 'landed' in New Jersey
events.notificationBody: In 1938, a radio drama of The War of the Worlds fooled some listeners.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - War of the Worlds (radio drama, 1938)

events.title: Ali defeats Foreman in the Rumble in the Jungle
events.summary: Muhammad Ali regains the heavyweight title in Kinshasa.
events.description: On October 30, 1974, in Kinshasa, Zaire, Muhammad Ali knocked out heavyweight champion George Foreman in the eighth round to reclaim the world heavyweight title, after using the tactic later dubbed 'rope-a-dope'.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Rumble in the Jungle

events.title: Tsar Nicholas II issues the October Manifesto
events.dateNote: October 17 in the Julian calendar then used in Russia.
events.summary: Russia's emperor promises a constitution and an elected Duma.
events.description: On October 30, 1905 (October 17 in Russia's Julian calendar), Tsar Nicholas II, on the advice of Sergey Witte, issued the October Manifesto, promising a constitution and an elected legislature, the Duma.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - October Manifesto

events.title: The Armistice of Mudros ends the Ottoman war
events.summary: The Ottoman Empire's defeat in World War I is sealed on the island of Lemnos.
events.description: On October 30, 1918, the Ottoman Empire and Great Britain, representing the Allied powers, signed an armistice at the port of Mudros on the Aegean island of Lemnos, marking the Ottoman defeat in World War I.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Armistice of Mudros

events.title: Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses
events.dateNote: Julian calendar date; the posting itself is traditional and not firmly documented.
events.summary: The traditional date for the start of the Protestant Reformation.
events.description: According to tradition, on October 31, 1517, Martin Luther posted his Ninety-five Theses on the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg. The theses came to be seen as the beginning of the Protestant Reformation, and October 31 is marked as Reformation Day.
events.notificationTitle: The theses that sparked the Reformation
events.notificationBody: In 1517, Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses set the Reformation in motion.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Ninety-five Theses

events.title: Nevada becomes the 36th state
events.summary: Admitted during the Civil War, Nevada becomes the 'Battle Born' state.
events.description: On October 31, 1864, during the American Civil War, Nevada became the 36th state in the Union. Its nickname, the Battle Born State, reflects that wartime admission.

sources.name: Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records - Nevada in the Civil War

events.title: The UN marks a world population of 7 billion
events.summary: UN projections put the global population at seven billion on this day.
events.description: October 31, 2011, was the date on which the United Nations projected that world population would reach 7 billion, based on its official World Population Prospects.

sources.name: United Nations Population Fund - World Population to Reach 7 Billion on 31 October

events.title: Indira Gandhi is assassinated
events.summary: India's first female prime minister is killed in New Delhi.
events.description: On October 31, 1984, Indira Gandhi, India's first female prime minister, was assassinated in New Delhi during her fourth term in office.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Indira Gandhi

events.title: The European Union is born
events.summary: The Maastricht Treaty enters into force and creates the EU.
events.description: On November 1, 1993, the Maastricht Treaty entered into force, creating the European Union. The treaty had been signed on February 7, 1992, and ratified by all member states of the European Community.
events.notificationTitle: The day the EU came into being
events.notificationBody: In 1993, the Maastricht Treaty took effect and created the European Union.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Maastricht Treaty

events.title: An earthquake devastates Lisbon
events.summary: A series of quakes strikes the Portuguese capital on All Saints' Day.
events.description: On the morning of November 1, 1755, a series of earthquakes caused serious damage to Lisbon. Because it was All Saints' Day, many people were at mass when churches collapsed.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Lisbon earthquake of 1755

events.title: An Italian pilot carries out the first aerial bombing
events.summary: Nine days after the first reconnaissance flight, a plane drops bombs in Libya.
events.description: On November 1, 1911, during the Italian-Ottoman war in Libya, Second Lieutenant Giulio Gavotti carried out the first aerial bombardment from an Etrich Taube aircraft.

sources.name: Smithsonian Air & Space Magazine - The World's First Warplane

events.title: Antigua and Barbuda becomes independent
events.summary: The Caribbean nation becomes an independent state within the Commonwealth.
events.description: On November 1, 1981, Antigua and Barbuda became an independent state within the Commonwealth of Nations, with Vere Cornwall Bird as its first prime minister.

sources.name: U.S. Office of the Historian - Antigua and Barbuda

events.title: The first crew moves into the International Space Station
events.summary: Expedition 1 begins a continuous human presence aboard the station.
events.description: On November 2, 2000, the Expedition 1 crew of American astronaut William Shepherd and Russian cosmonauts Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev arrived at the International Space Station, becoming the first people to live aboard it.
events.notificationTitle: Moving day in orbit
events.notificationBody: In 2000, the first crew moved into the International Space Station.

sources.name: NASA - Celebrating 20 Years on Station: Expedition 1
NASA - Expedition 1

events.title: Britain issues the Balfour Declaration
events.summary: A letter from the foreign secretary supports a Jewish national home in Palestine.
events.description: On November 2, 1917, British Foreign Secretary Arthur James Balfour wrote to Lionel Walter Rothschild, a leader of the Anglo-Jewish community, stating British support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Balfour Declaration

events.title: Haile Selassie is crowned emperor of Ethiopia
events.summary: Ras Tafari takes the throne and the name 'Might of the Trinity'.
events.description: On November 2, 1930, following the death of Empress Zauditu, Ras Tafari was crowned emperor of Ethiopia and took the name Haile Selassie, meaning 'Might of the Trinity'.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Haile Selassie I

events.title: The BBC launches regular television broadcasts
events.summary: The world's first regular high-definition TV service begins at Alexandra Palace.
events.description: On November 2, 1936, the BBC launched the world's first regular high-definition television service from studios at Alexandra Palace in London.

sources.name: Alexandra Palace - BBC at Alexandra Palace

events.title: Japan promulgates its postwar constitution
events.summary: A new constitution is proclaimed, to take effect six months later.
events.description: On November 3, 1946, the Constitution of Japan was promulgated, amending the Imperial Japanese Constitution through the Imperial Diet. It was set to take effect six months after promulgation.
events.notificationTitle: A new charter for postwar Japan
events.notificationBody: In 1946, Japan promulgated the constitution it still uses today.

sources.name: National Diet Library, Japan - Birth of the Constitution of Japan: The Constitution of Japan

events.title: Laika becomes the first animal to orbit Earth
events.summary: A Soviet dog rides Sputnik 2 into orbit.
events.description: On November 3, 1957, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 2 carrying Laika, a dog that became the first living creature to be launched into Earth orbit.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Laika

events.title: Panama declares independence from Colombia
events.summary: A revolt establishes the Republic of Panama.
events.description: On November 3, 1903, Panamanians revolted against the Colombian government, declared an independent Republic of Panama, and set up a provisional governing junta. The United States recognized the new republic three days later.

sources.name: U.S. Office of the Historian - Panama

events.title: Dominica becomes independent
events.summary: The Caribbean island nation gains independence from Britain.
events.description: On November 3, 1978, Great Britain granted independence to the Commonwealth of Dominica.

sources.name: U.S. Office of the Historian - Dominica

events.title: Excavators find the first sign of Tutankhamun's tomb
events.summary: Howard Carter's team uncovers the start of a largely intact royal tomb.
events.description: On November 4, 1922, Howard Carter's team of largely Egyptian excavators found the first sign of what proved to be the tomb of Tutankhamun. The sealed doorway behind which lay the tomb's treasures was reached on November 26.
events.notificationTitle: The find that led to Tutankhamun
events.notificationBody: In 1922, excavators found the first sign of Tutankhamun's tomb.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Howard Carter

events.title: The scientific journal Nature publishes its first issue
events.summary: Norman Lockyer's weekly begins a long run at the center of science.
events.description: On November 4, 1869, the first issue of the journal Nature was published, with Norman Lockyer as its first editor and Alexander Macmillan as publisher.

sources.name: Nature - History of Nature

events.title: Militants seize the US embassy in Tehran
events.summary: The start of a hostage crisis that lasts 444 days.
events.description: On November 4, 1979, a crowd attacked the US embassy in Tehran and took Americans hostage. More than 50 of them were held for 444 days.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Iran hostage crisis

events.title: Barack Obama is elected US president
events.summary: The president-elect addresses an election-night crowd in Chicago.
events.description: On November 4, 2008, Barack Obama won the US presidential election and addressed an election-night rally in Chicago's Grant Park as president-elect.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Barack Obama

events.title: The Gunpowder Plot is foiled
events.summary: A conspiracy to blow up Parliament and King James I fails.
events.description: November 5, 1605, was the day a group of English Roman Catholic conspirators planned to blow up Parliament and King James I at its opening. The plot was foiled, and in January 1606 Parliament made November 5 a day of public thanksgiving.
events.notificationTitle: Remember, remember
events.notificationBody: In 1605, the Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament was foiled.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Gunpowder Plot

events.title: Cal Rodgers completes the first flight across the United States
events.summary: The Vin Fiz lands in Pasadena after 49 days on the way from New York.
events.description: On November 5, 1911, Calbraith Perry Rodgers landed his Wright biplane, the Vin Fiz, in Pasadena's Tournament Park before about 20,000 people, completing the first flight across the United States. He had left Sheepshead Bay, New York, on September 17.

sources.name: Caltech Library - Cal Rodgers and his Vin Fiz
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum - Wright EX Vin Fiz

events.title: British and French troops land at Suez
events.summary: Anglo-French forces begin occupying the canal zone during the Suez Crisis.
events.description: On November 5, 1956, during the Suez Crisis, British and French forces began landing at Port Said and Port Fuad in Egypt and started occupying the Suez Canal zone.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Suez Crisis

events.title: The Battle of Inkerman is fought in the Crimea
events.summary: A major engagement of the Crimean War.
events.description: On November 5, 1854, the Battle of Inkerman was fought during the Crimean War, a significant engagement of the conflict.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Battle of Inkerman

events.title: Abraham Lincoln is elected president
events.summary: A divided nation elects Lincoln with under 40 percent of the popular vote.
events.description: On November 6, 1860, a deeply divided United States went to the polls and elected Abraham Lincoln president. He won slightly less than 40 percent of the popular vote but a majority of 180 electoral votes, sweeping the North and winning California and Oregon.
events.notificationTitle: The election that preceded the Civil War
events.notificationBody: In 1860, Abraham Lincoln won the US presidency with under 40% of the vote.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - U.S. Presidential Election of 1860

events.title: Rutgers and Princeton play the first college football game
events.summary: Rutgers wins the first intercollegiate football game, 6-4.
events.description: On November 6, 1869, Rutgers and Princeton played the first collegiate football game, in New Brunswick, New Jersey. Rutgers won 6-4.

sources.name: Rutgers University - The Birthplace of College Football

events.title: Australians vote on becoming a republic
events.summary: A referendum proposal to replace the monarchy with a president fails.
events.description: On November 6, 1999, Australians voted in a referendum on whether to make the country a republic with a president appointed by Parliament in place of the Queen and Governor-General. The proposal was not approved by the required double majority, and only the Australian Capital Territory recorded a majority 'yes' vote.

sources.name: Australian Electoral Commission - 1999 Referendum
Australian Electoral Commission - 1999 Referendum: Key results

events.title: Gustavus Adolphus dies at the Battle of Lutzen
events.dateNote: November 6 in the Julian calendar; November 16 in the Gregorian calendar.
events.summary: Sweden's warrior king is killed in a major battle of the Thirty Years' War.
events.description: On November 6, 1632 (by the Julian calendar then used in Sweden), Swedish forces fought imperial troops at Lutzen in Saxony during the Thirty Years' War. King Gustavus II Adolphus of Sweden was killed in the battle.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Battle of Lutzen

events.title: Marie Curie is born in Warsaw
events.summary: The future two-time Nobel laureate is born in Poland.
events.description: On November 7, 1867, Marie Curie was born in Warsaw. The Polish-born French physicist became famous for her work on radioactivity and won the Nobel Prize twice.
events.notificationTitle: Born to change science twice over
events.notificationBody: In 1867, Marie Curie, later a two-time Nobel laureate, was born in Warsaw.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Marie Curie

events.title: The last spike completes the Canadian Pacific Railway
events.summary: A ceremony in British Columbia marks Canada's first transcontinental railway.
events.description: On the morning of November 7, 1885, company director Donald Smith drove the ceremonial last spike of the Canadian Pacific Railway at Craigellachie, British Columbia, marking the completion of the transcontinental line.

sources.name: The Canadian Encyclopedia - The Last Spike

events.title: The Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd
events.dateNote: October 25 in the Julian calendar, hence the 'October Revolution'.
events.summary: Russia's October Revolution takes place as the Congress of Soviets convenes.
events.description: On November 7, 1917 (October 25 in Russia's Julian calendar), the Congress of Soviets convened in Petrograd as the Bolsheviks moved to take power. In an all-night session it declared government power vested in a Council of People's Commissars led by Lenin.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Russian Revolution

events.title: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapses
events.summary: 'Galloping Gertie' collapses in high winds.
events.description: On November 7, 1940, after strong winds blew through the Narrows, the Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington State, nicknamed 'Galloping Gertie', collapsed.

sources.name: Washington State Department of Transportation - Tacoma Narrows Bridge history: Collapse

events.title: Wilhelm Rontgen discovers X-rays
events.summary: A glowing screen in a German lab reveals a new kind of radiation.
events.description: On November 8, 1895, while experimenting with a cathode-ray tube, German physicist Wilhelm Rontgen noticed that a screen far from the tube glowed when the tube was operating, leading to his discovery of X-rays.
events.notificationTitle: The glow that revealed X-rays
events.notificationBody: In 1895, Wilhelm Rontgen stumbled on X-rays in his lab.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen

events.title: Hernan Cortes enters Tenochtitlan
events.summary: The Spanish force reaches the Aztec capital despite Montezuma's efforts to keep it away.
events.description: On November 8, 1519, Hernan Cortes entered Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital later rebuilt as Mexico City, with his small Spanish force and about 1,000 Tlaxcaltec allies.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Hernan Cortes

events.title: John F. Kennedy is elected president
events.summary: Kennedy narrowly defeats Richard Nixon.
events.description: On November 8, 1960, Democrat John F. Kennedy narrowly defeated Republican Vice President Richard Nixon to win the US presidency. He became the first Roman Catholic and the youngest person ever elected president.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - United States presidential election of 1960

events.title: Hitler's Beer Hall Putsch begins in Munich
events.summary: An attempted uprising against the Weimar Republic fails within a day.
events.description: On November 8, 1923, Adolf Hitler and Erich Ludendorff launched an attempt in Munich to start an insurrection against Germany's Weimar Republic. The Beer Hall Putsch failed the next day.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Beer Hall Putsch

events.title: The Berlin Wall opens
events.summary: East Germany opens its borders and crowds bring down the Cold War's great symbol.
events.description: On November 9, 1989, the East German government opened the country's borders, including those with West Berlin, and thousands of jubilant Germans began to bring down the Berlin Wall, the most visible symbol of Europe's division.
events.notificationTitle: The night the Wall opened
events.notificationBody: In 1989, East Germany opened its borders and the Berlin Wall began to fall.

sources.name: U.S. Office of the Historian - Fall of Communism in Eastern Europe, 1989
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Berlin Wall

events.title: Napoleon's Brumaire coup begins
events.summary: A two-day coup topples France's Directory and opens the way for Bonaparte.
events.description: On November 9, 1799 (18 Brumaire in the French Revolutionary calendar), the coup that overthrew France's Directory began, moving the legislature to Saint-Cloud under the pressure of Napoleon Bonaparte's troops. It replaced the Directory with the Consulate.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Coup of 18-19 Brumaire

events.title: Kaiser Wilhelm II is forced to abdicate
events.summary: Germany's last emperor gives up the throne and goes into exile.
events.description: On November 9, 1918, in the final days of World War I, Germany's Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to abdicate and was persuaded to seek asylum in the Netherlands.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Wilhelm II

events.title: The first Saturn V rocket flies
events.summary: The uncrewed Apollo 4 mission tests the rocket that would carry astronauts to the Moon.
events.description: On November 9, 1967, NASA launched the uncrewed Apollo 4 mission, the first all-up test of the three-stage Saturn V rocket. The flight tested the translunar motors and the high-speed reentry needed for crews returning from the Moon.

sources.name: NASA - Apollo 4

events.title: Luna 17 launches the first rover to the Moon
events.summary: The Soviet mission carries Lunokhod 1, which lands a week later.
events.description: On November 10, 1970, the Soviet Union launched Luna 17. It landed on the Moon's Mare Imbrium on November 17 and carried the lunar rover Lunokhod 1.
events.notificationTitle: A robot rover heads for the Moon
events.notificationBody: In 1970, Luna 17 launched carrying Lunokhod 1, the first lunar rover.

sources.name: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive - Soviet Missions to the Moon

events.title: Martin Luther is born
events.summary: The future catalyst of the Protestant Reformation is born in Eisleben.
events.description: On November 10, 1483, Martin Luther was born in Eisleben, Saxony. The German theologian and religious reformer became the catalyst of the 16th-century Protestant Reformation.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Martin Luther

events.title: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk dies
events.summary: The founder and first president of the Republic of Turkey dies in Istanbul.
events.description: On November 10, 1938, Kemal Ataturk, the soldier, statesman, and reformer who founded the Republic of Turkey and served as its first president from 1923, died in Istanbul.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Kemal Ataturk

events.title: The Armistice ends the fighting of World War I
events.summary: The guns fall silent on the Western Front at 11 a.m.
events.description: On November 11, 1918, Germany signed an armistice with the Allies, and the guns on the Western Front fell silent at 11 a.m., ending the fighting of the First World War in Western Europe.
events.notificationTitle: The eleventh hour of the eleventh day
events.notificationBody: In 1918, the guns of World War I fell silent at 11 a.m.

sources.name: Imperial War Museums - Armistice

events.title: Angola becomes independent
events.summary: Portugal grants independence as rival movements fight for control.
events.description: On November 11, 1975, Portugal granted Angola independence, at a time when several Angolan nationalist movements were fighting among themselves for control of the new state.

sources.name: U.S. Office of the Historian - Angola

events.title: Poland regains its independence
events.summary: Jozef Pilsudski takes power in Warsaw as World War I ends.
events.description: On November 11, 1918, as fighting in Western Europe ended, Jozef Pilsudski, newly arrived in Warsaw from Magdeburg, took power and became provisional head of the reborn Polish state. Poland marks the date as its National Independence Day.

sources.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Poland - 103rd anniversary of regaining independence

events.title: Pilgrims sign the Mayflower Compact
events.dateNote: November 11 in the Julian calendar; November 21 in the Gregorian calendar.
events.summary: Passengers sign a compact aboard ship before landing at Plymouth.
events.description: On November 11, 1620, by the Julian calendar then in use in England, passengers aboard the Mayflower signed the Mayflower Compact before landing at Plymouth, Massachusetts.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Mayflower Compact

events.title: Philae makes the first landing on a comet
events.summary: ESA's lander touches down on comet 67P after a ten-year journey.
events.description: On November 12, 2014, after a ten-year journey of more than 500 million kilometers, the European Space Agency's Rosetta lander Philae touched down on a comet, the first spacecraft ever to do so.
events.notificationTitle: Touchdown on a comet
events.notificationBody: In 2014, ESA's Philae became the first spacecraft to land on a comet.

sources.name: European Space Agency - Philae's extraordinary comet landing relived

events.title: Voyager 1 makes its closest approach to Saturn
events.summary: The probe passes about 126,000 km from the ringed planet.
events.description: On November 12, 1980, NASA's Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Saturn, passing at a range of about 126,000 kilometers (78,000 miles).

sources.name: NASA Science - Voyager 1

events.title: Sun Yat-sen is born
events.summary: The man known as the father of modern China is born in Guangdong.
events.description: On November 12, 1866, Sun Yat-sen was born in Xiangshan, Guangdong province. He led the Chinese Nationalist Party and is known as the father of modern China.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Sun Yat-sen

events.title: Akihito is formally enthroned as emperor of Japan
events.summary: Japan holds the enthronement ceremony for its new emperor.
events.description: On November 12, 1990, Akihito was formally enthroned as emperor of Japan.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Akihito

events.title: Robert Louis Stevenson is born
events.summary: The author of Treasure Island and Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde is born in Scotland.
events.description: On November 13, 1850, the Scottish essayist, poet, and novelist Robert Louis Stevenson was born. He became best known for Treasure Island, Kidnapped, and The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.
events.notificationTitle: The storyteller behind Treasure Island
events.notificationBody: In 1850, Robert Louis Stevenson was born in Scotland.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 13

events.title: The Supreme Court strikes down Montgomery's bus segregation
events.summary: The ruling vindicates the Montgomery bus boycott.
events.description: On November 13, 1956, the US Supreme Court affirmed a lower-court ruling in Browder v. Gayle that bus segregation in Alabama was unconstitutional. Martin Luther King, Jr., learned of the decision while on trial over the Montgomery bus boycott's carpools; the boycott ended the following month after 381 days.

sources.name: Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute (Stanford) - Browder v. Gayle

events.title: The Vietnam Veterans Memorial is dedicated
events.summary: Maya Lin's black granite wall is dedicated in Washington, D.C.
events.description: On November 13, 1982, the Vietnam Veterans Memorial was dedicated in Washington, D.C. Designed by Yale architecture student Maya Lin, its polished granite walls bear the names of more than 58,000 fallen men and women.

sources.name: The Cultural Landscape Foundation - Vietnam Veterans Memorial

events.title: Augustine of Hippo is born in North Africa
events.summary: The author of Confessions and The City of God is born in Numidia.
events.description: On November 13, 354, Augustine was born in Numidia, in what is now Algeria. The author of Confessions and The City of God, he served as bishop of Hippo and became one of the most significant Christian thinkers.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 13

events.title: Ruby Bridges walks into an all-white school
events.summary: A six-year-old begins integrating a New Orleans elementary school.
events.description: On November 14, 1960, six-year-old Ruby Bridges began attending an all-white elementary school in New Orleans, becoming the youngest of a group of Black students to racially integrate schools in the American South.
events.notificationTitle: Six years old and making history
events.notificationBody: In 1960, Ruby Bridges began integrating a New Orleans school.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 14

events.title: Nellie Bly sets out to beat Phileas Fogg
events.summary: The journalist races around the world in about 72 days.
events.description: On November 14, 1889, American journalist Nellie Bly began her race around the world against the fictional record of Phileas Fogg from Jules Verne's Around the World in Eighty Days. She completed the journey in slightly more than 72 days.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 14

events.title: Mariner 9 becomes the first spacecraft to orbit another planet
events.dateNote: Orbit insertion at 00:18 UTC; the evening of November 13 in US time zones.
events.summary: NASA's probe fires its engine and enters orbit around Mars.
events.description: On November 14, 1971 (UTC), NASA's Mariner 9 fired its main engine for more than 15 minutes and entered orbit around Mars, becoming the first human-made object to orbit another planet.

sources.name: NASA Science - Mariner 9

events.title: Clement V is crowned, the first Avignon pope
events.summary: A new pope begins the era of the papacy at Avignon.
events.description: On November 14, 1305, Clement V was crowned pope, becoming the first of the Avignon popes.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 14

events.title: The League of Nations holds its first Assembly
events.summary: Forty-one member states meet in Geneva for the new world body's opening session.
events.description: On November 15, 1920, 41 member states gathered in Geneva for the opening of the first session of the League of Nations Assembly, representing more than 70 percent of the world's population.
events.notificationTitle: The world's first parliament of nations
events.notificationBody: In 1920, the League of Nations Assembly met for the first time in Geneva.

sources.name: United Nations Office at Geneva - The League of Nations

events.title: Virat Kohli scores a record 50th ODI century
events.summary: India's batter breaks Sachin Tendulkar's long-standing one-day record.
events.description: On November 15, 2023, Virat Kohli scored his 50th century in one-day international cricket for India, breaking a record held by Sachin Tendulkar that many thought would never be broken.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 15

events.title: Georgia O'Keeffe is born
events.summary: The modernist painter of flowers, skulls, and desert landscapes is born.
events.description: On November 15, 1887, American painter Georgia O'Keeffe was born. A hugely influential Modernist, she became known for large-format paintings of flowers, skulls, shells, rocks, mountains, and other natural forms.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 15

events.title: King Gillette patents the disposable-blade razor
events.summary: A US patent covers the first razor with disposable blades.
events.description: On November 15, 1904, American inventor King Camp Gillette was granted a US patent for the first razor with disposable blades.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 15

events.title: Benazir Bhutto is elected prime minister of Pakistan
events.summary: She becomes the first woman in modern history to lead a Muslim country.
events.description: On November 16, 1988, Benazir Bhutto was elected prime minister of Pakistan, becoming the first woman in modern history to lead a Muslim country. She served from 1988 to 1990 and again from 1993 to 1996.
events.notificationTitle: A first for Pakistan and the Muslim world
events.notificationBody: In 1988, Benazir Bhutto was elected prime minister of Pakistan.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 16

events.title: David Livingstone reaches Victoria Falls
events.summary: The explorer becomes the first European to see Mosi-oa-Tunya.
events.description: On November 16, 1855, British explorer David Livingstone became the first European to see Victoria Falls, known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 16

events.title: Sint Eustatius salutes the United States
events.summary: A Caribbean island becomes the first foreign government to recognize the new nation.
events.description: On November 16, 1776, the Dutch Caribbean island of Sint Eustatius became the first foreign government to recognize the fledgling United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 16

events.title: Tiberius, future Roman emperor, is born
events.dateNote: Roman (pre-Julian reform) calendar date as traditionally given.
events.summary: The adopted son of Augustus and second Roman emperor is born.
events.description: On November 16, 42 BCE, Tiberius was born. The adopted son of Augustus, he became the second Roman emperor.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 16

events.title: The Suez Canal opens
events.summary: Egypt's great canal opens after ten years of construction.
events.description: On November 17, 1869, after 10 years of construction, the Suez Canal opened in Egypt.
events.notificationTitle: A canal a decade in the making
events.notificationBody: In 1869, the Suez Canal opened after ten years of construction.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 17

events.title: Protests in Prague begin the Velvet Revolution
events.summary: Mass demonstrations lead to the fall of Czechoslovakia's communist government.
events.description: On November 17, 1989, police brutality at a Prague demonstration marking the 50th anniversary of a student protest suppressed under German occupation set off massive antigovernment demonstrations in Czechoslovakia. Led by Vaclav Havel, they continued until the communist government resigned.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 17

events.title: Elizabeth I becomes queen of England
events.summary: The death of Mary I brings Elizabeth Tudor to the throne.
events.description: On November 17, 1558, on the death of Mary I, Elizabeth Tudor came to the English throne as Elizabeth I.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 17

events.title: Mickey Mouse stars in Steamboat Willie
events.summary: Disney releases the first Mickey Mouse cartoon with sound.
events.description: On November 18, 1928, Walt Disney released Steamboat Willie, the first animated film with sound to feature Mickey Mouse. Its success helped make Mickey an iconic character.
events.notificationTitle: Mickey Mouse finds his voice
events.notificationBody: In 1928, Steamboat Willie brought Mickey Mouse to the screen with sound.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 18

events.title: Latvia proclaims independence
events.summary: The Latvian People's Council declares a new state.
events.description: On November 18, 1918, the Latvian People's Council proclaimed Latvia's independence.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 18

events.title: Haitian forces win the Battle of Vertieres
events.summary: Victory over the French effectively ends the Haitian Revolution.
events.description: On November 18, 1803, Haitian forces led by Jean-Jacques Dessalines defeated the French at the Battle of Vertieres, effectively concluding the Haitian Revolution and opening the way to Haiti's declaration of independence weeks later.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 18

events.title: St. Peter's Basilica is consecrated
events.summary: The new basilica in Vatican City is dedicated.
events.description: On November 18, 1626, Saint Peter's Basilica in Vatican City, built to replace an earlier basilica, was consecrated.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 18

events.title: Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address
events.summary: A brief speech at a Civil War cemetery becomes one of history's most famous.
events.description: On November 19, 1863, during the American Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln delivered the brief but renowned Gettysburg Address at the dedication of the National Cemetery in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.
events.notificationTitle: A short speech for the ages
events.notificationBody: In 1863, Abraham Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 19

events.title: Anwar Sadat makes a historic visit to Israel
events.summary: Egypt's president travels to Israel and offers a peace plan.
events.description: On November 19, 1977, Egyptian President Anwar Sadat began a historic visit to Israel, during which he offered a peace plan to the Israeli parliament.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 19

events.title: Pele scores his 1,000th career goal
events.summary: The Brazilian football legend reaches a milestone.
events.description: On November 19, 1969, Brazilian football player Pele scored his 1,000th career goal.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 19

events.title: The Man in the Iron Mask dies in the Bastille
events.summary: A prisoner of legend dies in Paris.
events.description: On November 19, 1703, the Man in the Iron Mask, a political prisoner famous in French history and legend, died in the Bastille.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 19

events.title: Francisco Madero launches the Mexican Revolution
events.summary: A failed revolt inspires the leaders who topple Porfirio Diaz.
events.description: On November 20, 1910, Francisco Madero launched a revolt that failed but sparked the Mexican Revolution, inspiring leaders such as Pancho Villa and Emiliano Zapata to mobilize their armies against President Porfirio Diaz.
events.notificationTitle: The spark of the Mexican Revolution
events.notificationBody: In 1910, Francisco Madero's revolt set the Mexican Revolution in motion.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 20

events.title: The first World Cup in the Middle East kicks off
events.summary: Ecuador beats host Qatar in the opening match.
events.description: On November 20, 2022, the first FIFA World Cup held in the Middle East began in Qatar, with Ecuador defeating the host country in the opening match.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 20

events.title: A sperm whale rams the whaleship Essex
events.summary: The sinking later inspires the climax of Moby-Dick.
events.description: On November 20, 1820, the American whaling ship Essex was rammed by a sperm whale and later sank, an event that inspired the climactic scene of Herman Melville's Moby-Dick.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 20

events.title: Tanks are first used effectively at Cambrai
events.summary: British armor changes the character of World War I battle.
events.description: On November 20, 1917, at the Battle of Cambrai during World War I, the British used tanks effectively in warfare for the first time.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 20

events.title: The first crewed hot-air balloon flight
events.summary: Two Frenchmen float over Paris in a Montgolfier balloon.
events.description: On November 21, 1783, Jean-Francois Pilatre de Rozier and the marquis d'Arlandes made the first crewed hot-air balloon flight, traveling from the Chateau de la Muette across the Bois de Boulogne near Paris in a balloon built by the Montgolfier brothers.
events.notificationTitle: The first people to fly
events.notificationBody: In 1783, two Frenchmen made the first crewed hot-air balloon flight.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 21

events.title: The Dayton Accords end the Bosnian War
events.summary: Leaders of Bosnia, Croatia, and Serbia reach a peace agreement.
events.description: On November 21, 1995, the presidents of Bosnia, Croatia, and Serbia reached the peace agreement known as the Dayton Accords, ending the Bosnian War.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 21

events.title: Voltaire is born
events.summary: The French writer famed for his satiric wit is born.
events.description: On November 21, 1694, Voltaire was born. One of the greatest French writers, he is remembered for his critical capacity and satiric wit and as a crusader against tyranny, bigotry, and cruelty.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 21

events.title: Robert Mugabe resigns in Zimbabwe
events.summary: The leader of 37 years steps down as impeachment begins.
events.description: On November 21, 2017, after some 37 years as leader of Zimbabwe, first as prime minister and later as president, Robert Mugabe resigned as parliament began impeachment proceedings against him.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 21

events.title: Toy Story, the first computer-animated feature, is released
events.summary: Pixar's film launches a new era of animation.
events.description: On November 22, 1995, Pixar's Toy Story, the first entirely computer-animated feature-length film, was released. It became a critical and commercial hit and started a long-running franchise.
events.notificationTitle: To infinity and the box office
events.notificationBody: In 1995, Toy Story became the first fully computer-animated feature film.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 22

events.title: President John F. Kennedy is assassinated
events.summary: The 35th US president is shot in Dallas.
events.description: On November 22, 1963, John F. Kennedy, the 35th president of the United States, was shot and killed in Dallas, Texas.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 22

events.title: Lebanon proclaims independence from France
events.summary: The declaration begins Lebanon's path to full sovereignty.
events.description: On November 22, 1943, Lebanon proclaimed its independence from France, though it did not become wholly independent until 1946.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 22

events.title: Angela Merkel becomes Germany's first woman chancellor
events.summary: She is sworn in to lead the German government.
events.description: On November 22, 2005, Angela Merkel was sworn in as chancellor of Germany, the first woman to hold the post.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 22

events.title: Doctor Who airs for the first time
events.summary: The BBC science-fiction series begins its long journey through time.
events.description: On November 23, 1963, the first episode of the British science-fiction series Doctor Who aired, and the show soon became a landmark of British popular culture.
events.notificationTitle: The Doctor's first journey
events.notificationBody: In 1963, Doctor Who aired its first episode on the BBC.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 23

events.title: Mexico passes the Ley Juarez
events.summary: Special courts for clergy and military are abolished.
events.description: On November 23, 1855, Mexico passed the Ley Juarez, which abolished special courts for the clergy and military in an effort by justice minister Benito Juarez to remove remnants of colonialism and promote equality.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 23

events.title: The first issue of Life magazine is published
events.summary: The weekly becomes a pioneer of photojournalism.
events.description: On November 23, 1936, the first issue of Life was published. The magazine became a pioneer in photojournalism and a major force in the field's development.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 23

events.title: Otto I, future Holy Roman emperor, is born
events.summary: The ruler who consolidated the German realm is born.
events.description: On November 23, 912, Otto I was born. As Holy Roman emperor he consolidated the German realm by suppressing rebellious vassals and winning a decisive victory over the Hungarians.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 23

events.title: Abel Tasman reaches Tasmania
events.summary: The Dutch navigator skirts the island's southern shores.
events.description: On November 24, 1642, Dutch navigator Abel Janszoon Tasman, sailing from Batavia (Jakarta) to seek an eastward sea passage to Chile and explore New Guinea, skirted the southern shores of Tasmania.
events.notificationTitle: A Dutch sighting at the edge of the world
events.notificationBody: In 1642, Abel Tasman reached the island now called Tasmania.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 24

events.title: Anna Sewell publishes Black Beauty
events.summary: Her only novel becomes a landmark animal story for children.
events.description: On November 24, 1877, shortly before her death, Anna Sewell published her only novel, Black Beauty, the first major story about an animal in children's literature.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 24

events.title: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec is born
events.summary: The artist of Parisian nightlife is born in France.
events.description: On November 24, 1864, the French artist Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was born. He documented Parisian nightlife and the world of entertainment in the 1890s with great psychological insight.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 24

events.title: Agatha Christie's The Mousetrap opens in London
events.summary: The mystery play begins a run that lasts for decades.
events.description: On November 25, 1952, Agatha Christie's play The Mousetrap opened in London. By its 50th anniversary in 2002, it had been performed more than 20,000 times.
events.notificationTitle: The play that never closed
events.notificationBody: In 1952, Agatha Christie's The Mousetrap opened in London.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 25

events.title: Suriname becomes independent
events.summary: The South American nation gains independence from the Netherlands.
events.description: On November 25, 1975, Suriname gained its independence from the Netherlands.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 25

events.title: Lope de Vega is born
events.summary: The Spanish author is born.
events.description: On November 25, 1562, the Spanish author Lope de Vega was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 25

events.title: Los Alamos is chosen for the atomic bomb project
events.summary: Groves and Oppenheimer pick a New Mexico mesa for Project Y.
events.description: On November 25, 1942, Leslie Groves and J. Robert Oppenheimer chose Los Alamos, New Mexico, as the site of Project Y, which developed the first atomic bomb.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 25

events.title: Casablanca premieres
events.summary: Bogart and Bergman's wartime romance becomes a Hollywood classic.
events.description: On November 26, 1942, Casablanca premiered. Set in occupied Morocco during World War II, directed by Michael Curtiz, and starring Humphrey Bogart, Ingrid Bergman, and Paul Henreid, it became one of Hollywood's most revered films.
events.notificationTitle: Here's looking at a classic
events.notificationBody: In 1942, Casablanca premiered and became a Hollywood legend.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 26

events.title: The Mongolian People's Republic is proclaimed
events.summary: A new state is declared after the defeat of White Russian and Chinese forces.
events.description: On November 26, 1924, after the defeat of the White Russians and the Chinese, the Mongolian People's Republic was proclaimed.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 26

events.title: The National Hockey League is founded
events.summary: The league begins with four Canadian teams.
events.description: On November 26, 1917, the National Hockey League was founded with four Canadian teams. Its first American club, the Boston Bruins, joined in 1924.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 26

events.title: NASA launches the Curiosity rover to Mars
events.summary: The rover lifts off from Cape Canaveral.
events.description: On November 26, 2011, NASA's Mars rover Curiosity was launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 26

events.title: Alfred Nobel's will creates the Nobel Prizes
events.summary: The inventor of dynamite's will creates the prizes.
events.description: On November 27, 1895, the Nobel Prizes were established through the will of Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist, engineer, and industrialist who invented dynamite and other powerful explosives.
events.notificationTitle: The will behind the Nobel Prizes
events.notificationBody: In 1895, Alfred Nobel's will established the Nobel Prizes.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 27

events.title: The first Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
events.summary: A New York tradition begins; the giant balloons arrive three years later.
events.description: On November 27, 1924, the first Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was held in New York City. It became an American tradition, known especially for the huge balloons introduced in 1927.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 27

events.title: The Treaty of Neuilly sets peace terms for Bulgaria
events.summary: Bulgaria and the Allies sign a post-World War I settlement.
events.description: On November 27, 1919, the Treaty of Neuilly, setting out the post-World War I peace terms for Bulgaria, was signed between Bulgaria and the Allied powers.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 27

events.title: Anders Celsius is born
events.dateNote: Date as given by Britannica; Sweden then used its own transitional calendar.
events.summary: The Swedish astronomer is born.
events.description: On November 27, 1701, the Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 27

events.title: Albania declares independence
events.summary: Delegates at Vlore proclaim an independent Albania.
events.description: On November 28, 1912, Albanian national delegates led by Ismail Qemal issued the Vlore proclamation, declaring Albania's independence.
events.notificationTitle: Albania's day of independence
events.notificationBody: In 1912, Albania declared its independence at Vlore.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 28

events.title: Mauritania declares independence
events.summary: The West African country leaves the French Community.
events.description: On November 28, 1960, Mauritania declared its independence and left the French Community.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 28

events.title: The Tehran Conference opens
events.summary: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin meet in Iran.
events.description: On November 28, 1943, the Tehran Conference opened, bringing together US President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin, who pressed for an invasion of France.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 28

events.title: Richard Byrd flies over the South Pole
events.summary: An American aviator crosses the bottom of the world by air.
events.description: On November 29, 1929, American pioneer aviator Richard E. Byrd flew over the South Pole.
events.notificationTitle: Flying over the bottom of the world
events.notificationBody: In 1929, Richard Byrd flew over the South Pole.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 29

events.title: Polish cadets launch the November Insurrection
events.summary: An uprising in Warsaw challenges Russian rule.
events.description: On November 29, 1830, a Polish secret society of infantry cadets staged an uprising in Warsaw, beginning the November Insurrection.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 29

events.title: Louisa May Alcott is born
events.summary: The author of Little Women is born in Pennsylvania.
events.description: On November 29, 1832, Louisa May Alcott, best known for her novel Little Women, was born in Pennsylvania.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 29

events.title: The UN votes to partition Palestine
events.summary: Resolution 181 proposes Arab and Jewish states and an international Jerusalem.
events.description: On November 29, 1947, the United Nations General Assembly passed Resolution 181, which called for the partition of Palestine into Arab and Jewish states and for placing Jerusalem under a special international regime.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 29

events.title: Barbados becomes independent
events.summary: The Caribbean island gains full independence from Britain.
events.description: On November 30, 1966, Barbados, which had gained internal self-rule in 1961, achieved full independence from Britain.
events.notificationTitle: Barbados becomes a nation
events.notificationBody: In 1966, Barbados achieved full independence from Britain.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 30

events.title: Britain and the US sign preliminary peace articles
events.summary: The first step toward ending the American Revolution is agreed in Paris.
events.description: On November 30, 1782, Britain and the United States signed the preliminary articles of the Treaty of Paris, part of the Peace of Paris that concluded the American Revolution.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 30

events.title: Michael Jackson releases Thriller
events.summary: It becomes the best-selling album in the world.
events.description: On November 30, 1982, Michael Jackson released Thriller, which became the best-selling album in the world and won a record eight Grammy Awards.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 30

events.title: The Stone of Scone returns to Scotland
events.summary: The coronation stone comes home 700 years after Edward I took it.
events.description: On November 30, 1996, the Stone of Scone, a block of gray sandstone, was returned to Scotland 700 years after King Edward I took it to England as war booty.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 30

events.title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat
events.summary: Her arrest in Montgomery sparks a 381-day boycott.
events.description: On December 1, 1955, in Montgomery, Alabama, Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat to a white passenger in violation of segregation laws and was arrested, sparking a 381-day bus boycott led by Martin Luther King, Jr.
events.notificationTitle: One seat, a movement
events.notificationBody: In 1955, Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 1

events.title: Ford debuts the moving assembly line
events.summary: Model T production is transformed at Highland Park, Michigan.
events.description: On December 1, 1913, the world's first moving assembly line debuted at a Ford factory in Highland Park, Michigan, manufacturing Model Ts. Henry Ford's innovation revolutionized the auto industry.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 1

events.title: The first World AIDS Day is held
events.summary: A global day of awareness begins.
events.description: On December 1, 1988, the first World AIDS Day was held.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 1

events.title: The Pact of Locarno is signed
events.summary: Five European powers sign agreements meant to secure peace in western Europe.
events.description: On December 1, 1925, Germany, France, Belgium, Great Britain, and Italy signed the Pact of Locarno, a series of agreements intended to guarantee peace in western Europe.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 1

events.title: Scientists achieve the first controlled nuclear chain reaction
events.summary: Enrico Fermi's team makes history at the University of Chicago.
events.description: On December 2, 1942, scientists led by Enrico Fermi conducted the world's first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction at the University of Chicago.
events.notificationTitle: The day the atom was harnessed
events.notificationBody: In 1942, Enrico Fermi's team ran the first controlled nuclear chain reaction.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 2

events.title: The United Arab Emirates is formed
events.summary: Six emirates on the Arabian Peninsula unite.
events.description: On December 2, 1971, the United Arab Emirates was formed by the union of six small emirates on the Arabian Peninsula; a seventh joined in February 1972.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 2

events.title: Napoleon crowns himself emperor
events.summary: The ceremony in Paris takes place in the presence of the pope.
events.description: On December 2, 1804, Napoleon crowned himself emperor of France in the presence of Pope Pius VII.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 2

events.title: President Monroe sets out the Monroe Doctrine
events.summary: The US warns European powers away from the Western Hemisphere.
events.description: On December 2, 1823, in his annual message to Congress, President James Monroe declared that the United States would not interfere in European affairs and would treat any European attempt to control a nation in the Western Hemisphere as a hostile act. The policy became known as the Monroe Doctrine.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 2

events.title: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant
events.summary: A Cape Town surgical team makes medical history.
events.description: On December 3, 1967, South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the first human heart transplant, at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town.
events.notificationTitle: A new heart in Cape Town
events.notificationBody: In 1967, Christiaan Barnard performed the first human heart transplant.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 3

events.title: Gold miners fight at the Eureka Stockade
events.summary: Diggers in Victoria, Australia, clash with government forces.
events.description: On December 3, 1854, gold miners at the Eureka goldfield in Victoria, Australia, who had barricaded themselves inside a hastily built stockade, opened fire on the government forces surrounding them, the culmination of long-standing grievances.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 3

events.title: A Streetcar Named Desire opens on Broadway
events.summary: Tennessee Williams's play premieres with Marlon Brando.
events.description: On December 3, 1947, Tennessee Williams's A Streetcar Named Desire premiered on Broadway, starring Jessica Tandy, Kim Hunter, and Marlon Brando.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 3

events.title: Missionary Francis Xavier dies off the coast of China
events.summary: The leading Catholic missionary of his era dies of fever.
events.description: On December 3, 1552, St. Francis Xavier, the leading Roman Catholic missionary of modern times, died of fever off the coast of China.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 3

events.title: Mars Pathfinder launches
events.summary: NASA sends a lander to explore the Martian surface.
events.description: On December 4, 1996, the Mars Pathfinder spacecraft was launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida, to explore the surface of Mars.
events.notificationTitle: Next stop: the surface of Mars
events.notificationBody: In 1996, Mars Pathfinder launched to explore the Red Planet's surface.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 4

events.title: Three-year-old Ivan IV becomes grand prince of Moscow
events.summary: The future Ivan the Terrible inherits the throne as a child.
events.description: On December 4, 1533, on the death of his father, Grand Prince Vasily III, the three-year-old who would become Ivan the Terrible was proclaimed grand prince of Moscow. His mother ruled in his name until her death in 1538.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 4

events.title: The first Grey Cup is awarded
events.summary: The Toronto Varsity Blues win Canada's amateur football championship.
events.description: On December 4, 1909, the Grey Cup was awarded for the first time, as the Toronto Varsity Blues defeated the Toronto Parkdale team in Canada's amateur football championship game.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 4

events.title: Adrian IV becomes the only English pope
events.summary: An Englishman is elected to the papal throne.
events.description: On December 4, 1154, Adrian IV was elected pope, becoming the only Englishman ever to occupy the papal throne.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 4

events.title: Nelson Mandela dies
events.summary: South Africa's first Black president dies at 95.
events.description: On December 5, 2013, Nelson Mandela, who helped end South Africa's apartheid system and became the country's first Black president, died at the age of 95.
events.notificationTitle: Remembering Nelson Mandela
events.notificationBody: In 2013, Nelson Mandela, South Africa's first Black president, died at 95.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 5

events.title: Walt Disney is born
events.summary: The creator of Mickey Mouse is born in Chicago.
events.description: On December 5, 1901, Walt Disney was born in Chicago. He pioneered animated cartoon films, created characters such as Mickey Mouse and Donald Duck, and founded what became one of the world's largest entertainment companies.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 5

events.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart dies
events.summary: The composer dies in Vienna at 35.
events.description: On December 5, 1791, the Austrian composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart died in Vienna at the age of 35.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 5

events.title: The Anglo-Irish Treaty establishes the Irish Free State
events.summary: The agreement concludes the Irish War of Independence.
events.description: On December 6, 1921, representatives of the British government and Irish leaders including Arthur Griffith and Michael Collins signed the Anglo-Irish Treaty, concluding the Irish War of Independence and establishing the Irish Free State.
events.notificationTitle: The treaty that made the Irish Free State
events.notificationBody: In 1921, the Anglo-Irish Treaty was signed, creating the Irish Free State.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 6

events.title: Finland declares independence from Russia
events.summary: The declaration follows the Bolshevik Revolution.
events.description: On December 6, 1917, following the Bolshevik Revolution, Finland declared itself independent of Russia.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 6

events.title: The bust of Nefertiti is discovered
events.summary: Excavators at Tell el-Amarna uncover a famous sculpture.
events.description: On December 6, 1912, a bust of Nefertiti was discovered during excavations at Tell el-Amarna, Egypt. It later went on display in a Berlin museum, and calls for its repatriation have made it a source of controversy.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 6

events.title: A US judge rules Ulysses is not obscene
events.summary: The landmark decision opens the way for James Joyce's novel.
events.description: On December 6, 1933, in a landmark ruling, a US federal judge held that James Joyce's Ulysses was not obscene, allowing greater freedom for literary works.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 6

events.title: Apollo 17, the last crewed Moon mission, launches
events.summary: Eugene Cernan commands the final Apollo flight to the Moon.
events.description: On December 7, 1972, Apollo 17 launched on the Apollo program's last lunar landing mission, commanded by Eugene Cernan. It landed in the Moon's Taurus-Littrow Valley and was the first mission to include an astronaut-scientist.
events.notificationTitle: The last voyage to the Moon
events.notificationBody: In 1972, Apollo 17 set off on the last crewed Moon mission.

sources.name: NASA - Apollo 17
Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 7

events.title: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor
events.summary: A surprise air raid brings the United States into World War II.
events.description: On December 7, 1941, Japanese bombers launched a surprise attack on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor on Oahu, Hawaii, bringing the United States into World War II.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 7

events.title: Delaware becomes the first state to ratify the Constitution
events.summary: Delaware is first to approve the new US Constitution.
events.description: On December 7, 1787, Delaware became the first state to ratify the US Constitution.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 7

events.title: Gian Lorenzo Bernini is born
events.summary: The sculptor-architect who shaped the Baroque is born.
events.description: On December 7, 1598, Gian Lorenzo Bernini was born. Perhaps the greatest sculptor-architect of the 17th century, he created the Baroque style and produced masterpieces such as The Ecstasy of St. Teresa.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 7

events.title: Notre-Dame Cathedral reopens
events.summary: Paris's cathedral welcomes the public again after the 2019 fire.
events.description: On December 8, 2024, the restored Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris reopened to the public, a little more than five years after it was heavily damaged by fire.
events.notificationTitle: Notre-Dame opens its doors again
events.notificationBody: In 2024, Paris's Notre-Dame reopened five years after the fire.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 8

events.title: SpaceX's Dragon returns from orbit
events.summary: A private company recovers a spacecraft from orbit for the first time.
events.description: On December 8, 2010, SpaceX became the first commercial company to launch a spacecraft, the Dragon capsule, into orbit and successfully return it to Earth.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 8

events.title: Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus agree to form the CIS
events.summary: The Commonwealth of Independent States emerges as the Soviet Union ends.
events.description: On December 8, 1991, Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus signed an agreement to form the Commonwealth of Independent States in the wake of the Soviet Union's demise.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 8

events.title: Diego Rivera is born
events.summary: The Mexican muralist who revived fresco painting is born.
events.description: On December 8, 1886, Diego Rivera was born in Mexico. His bold, large-scale murals stimulated a revival of fresco painting in Latin America.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 8

events.title: Smallpox is declared eradicated
events.summary: A global vaccination campaign defeats the disease.
events.description: On December 9, 1979, some 10 years after the World Health Organization began a global vaccination program against smallpox, the disease was officially declared eradicated.
events.notificationTitle: A disease wiped off the Earth
events.notificationBody: In 1979, smallpox was officially declared eradicated.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 9

events.title: Tanganyika becomes independent
events.summary: Julius Nyerere becomes the first prime minister of the future Tanzania.
events.description: On December 9, 1961, Tanganyika became independent, with Julius Nyerere as its first prime minister. In 1964 it united with Zanzibar to form Tanzania.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 9

events.title: Sucre defeats the Spanish at Ayacucho
events.summary: A decisive revolutionary victory in South America.
events.description: On December 9, 1824, revolutionary forces led by Antonio Jose de Sucre defeated the Spanish royal army at the Battle of Ayacucho.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 9

events.title: The world's first traffic light goes up in London
events.summary: A gas-lit signal near Westminster Bridge lasts only a month.
events.description: On December 9, 1868, the world's first traffic light was erected near Westminster Bridge in London. It was removed a month later after a gas leak caused one of its lights to explode.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 9

events.title: The UN adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
