events.summary: The General Assembly sets out rights for all people.
events.description: On December 10, 1948, the United Nations General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
events.notificationTitle: Rights for every human being
events.notificationBody: In 1948, the UN adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 10

events.title: The first Nobel Prizes are awarded
events.summary: The prizes are presented on the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.
events.description: On December 10, 1901, the first Nobel Prizes were distributed, on the fifth anniversary of the death of Alfred Nobel, who founded and endowed the awards through his will.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 10

events.title: Ada Lovelace is born
events.summary: The woman often called the first computer programmer is born in London.
events.description: On December 10, 1815, Ada Lovelace, often considered the first computer programmer, was born in what is now London.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 10

events.title: Australia gives up its 'Emu War'
events.summary: A month-long military campaign against flightless birds ends.
events.description: On December 10, 1932, the Australian government officially gave up after a month-long campaign against thousands of emus, an episode known as the Emu War.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 10

events.title: Mandela signs South Africa's democratic constitution
events.summary: The new constitution completes the transition from apartheid.
events.description: On December 10, 1996, President Nelson Mandela signed South Africa's new constitution, completing the transition from white minority rule under apartheid to full democracy.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 10

events.title: UNICEF is established
events.summary: The UN creates a program for the world's children.
events.description: On December 11, 1946, UNICEF, a United Nations program devoted to improving the health, nutrition, education, and general welfare of children, was established.
events.notificationTitle: A UN agency for every child
events.notificationBody: In 1946, the United Nations established UNICEF.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 11

events.title: Edward VIII's abdication takes effect
events.summary: The king gives up the throne to marry Wallis Simpson.
events.description: On December 11, 1936, the abdication of Edward VIII as king of the United Kingdom was formally approved. He remains the only British sovereign to give up the crown voluntarily, which he did to marry the American divorcee Wallis Warfield Simpson.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 11

events.title: Naguib Mahfouz is born in Cairo
events.summary: The first Arabic-language Nobel laureate in literature is born.
events.description: On December 11, 1911, Naguib Mahfouz, who would become the first Arabic writer awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature, was born in Cairo.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 11

events.title: Swiss Catholic cantons form the Sonderbund
events.summary: The league leads to a brief Swiss civil war in 1847.
events.description: On December 11, 1845, seven conservative Roman Catholic Swiss cantons formed the Sonderbund to oppose anti-Catholic measures by the Protestant liberal cantons. The tensions ended in a brief civil war in 1847.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 11

events.title: Nations reach the Paris climate agreement
events.summary: 195 countries agree to limit greenhouse gas emissions.
events.description: On December 12, 2015, at a United Nations conference in Paris, 195 countries reached a landmark climate change agreement to limit greenhouse gas emissions; the accord effectively replaced the Kyoto Protocol.
events.notificationTitle: A global deal on climate
events.notificationBody: In 2015, 195 countries agreed the Paris climate accord.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 12

events.title: The world's first motel opens
events.summary: A roadside stop in California gives the 'mo-tel' its name.
events.description: On December 12, 1925, the world's first motel, the Milestone Mo-Tel, opened in San Luis Obispo, California, giving motorists a place to stop between San Francisco and Los Angeles.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 12

events.title: Kenya becomes a republic
events.summary: The change comes on the first anniversary of independence.
events.description: On December 12, 1964, Kenya became a republic on the first anniversary of its independence from Britain.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 12

events.title: Edvard Munch is born
events.summary: The painter of The Scream is born in Norway.
events.description: On December 12, 1863, the Norwegian artist Edvard Munch was born. His painting The Scream became a symbol of modern spiritual anguish, and his work influenced German Expressionism.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 12

events.title: Abel Tasman sights New Zealand
events.summary: The Dutch navigator is the first European to see the South Island.
events.description: On December 13, 1642, Dutch navigator Abel Tasman became the first European to sight the South Island of New Zealand.
events.notificationTitle: A first European sighting of New Zealand
events.notificationBody: In 1642, Abel Tasman sighted New Zealand's South Island.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 13

events.title: The Council of Trent opens
events.summary: The Catholic Church's response to the Reformation begins.
events.description: On December 13, 1545, the Council of Trent, the 19th ecumenical council of the Roman Catholic Church, opened in Trent, Italy. It helped revitalize the church in much of Europe after the Protestant Reformation.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 13

events.title: Pope Celestine V resigns
events.summary: A hermit pope steps down after five months.
events.description: On December 13, 1294, after five months as pope, Celestine V resigned. A former hermit struggling with his duties, he judged that continuing would endanger both the church and his soul.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 13

events.title: Nova Herculis flares into view
events.summary: One of the brightest novas of the 20th century is discovered.
events.description: On December 13, 1934, British astronomer J.P.M. Prentice discovered Nova Herculis, one of the brightest novas of the 20th century.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 13

events.title: Roald Amundsen reaches the South Pole
events.summary: The Norwegian explorer's team is the first to reach the pole.
events.description: On December 14, 1911, Roald Amundsen, traveling with four companions, 52 dogs, and four sledges, became the first explorer to reach the South Pole.
events.notificationTitle: First to the South Pole
events.notificationBody: In 1911, Roald Amundsen's team became the first to reach the South Pole.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 14

events.title: The OECD convention is signed
events.summary: Twenty countries sign on to a new economic organization.
events.description: On December 14, 1960, the convention establishing the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development was signed by 18 European countries, the United States, and Canada.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 14

events.title: Wilma Mankiller becomes principal chief of the Cherokee Nation
events.summary: She is the first woman to lead a major Native tribe.
events.description: On December 14, 1985, Wilma Mankiller was sworn in as principal chief of the Cherokee Nation, becoming the first woman to serve as chief of a major Native tribe.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 14

events.title: Tycho Brahe is born
events.summary: The Danish astronomer who mapped the stars before the telescope is born.
events.description: On December 14, 1546, the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe was born. He developed astronomical instruments and fixed the positions of stars before the invention of the telescope, paving the way for later discoveries.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 14

events.title: The US Bill of Rights is adopted
events.summary: The first ten amendments to the Constitution take effect together.
events.description: On December 15, 1791, the first 10 amendments to the US Constitution, known as the Bill of Rights, were adopted as a single unit, guaranteeing individual rights and limiting government.
events.notificationTitle: Ten amendments, one bill of rights
events.notificationBody: In 1791, the US Bill of Rights was adopted.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 15

events.title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa reopens
events.summary: The tower welcomes visitors again after a decade of stabilization work.
events.description: On December 15, 2001, the Leaning Tower of Pisa reopened after more than 10 years of work to stabilize the structure.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 15

events.title: Janet Jagan is elected president of Guyana
events.summary: She becomes South America's first elected female president.
events.description: On December 15, 1997, Janet Jagan was elected president of Guyana, becoming the first elected female president in South America.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 15

events.title: Nero, future Roman emperor, is born
events.summary: The future fifth Roman emperor is born.
events.description: On December 15, 37 CE, Nero was born. He became the fifth Roman emperor, infamous for his personal extravagance.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 15

events.title: The Boston Tea Party
events.summary: Protesters dump British East India Company tea into Boston Harbor.
events.description: On December 16, 1773, a group of men disguised in Mohawk headdresses, cheered by a crowd of thousands, threw tea belonging to the British East India Company into Boston Harbor in protest against taxes. Britain's punitive response helped push the American colonists closer to war.
events.notificationTitle: The tea that stirred a revolution
events.notificationBody: In 1773, colonists dumped British tea into Boston Harbor.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 16

events.title: Jane Austen is born
events.summary: The novelist of everyday English life is born.
events.description: On December 16, 1775, the English writer Jane Austen was born. Her novels of ordinary people in everyday life gave the novel its distinctly modern character.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 16

events.title: Oliver Cromwell becomes lord protector
events.summary: Cromwell takes the title as head of England, Scotland, and Ireland.
events.description: On December 16, 1653, Oliver Cromwell became lord protector of England, Scotland, and Ireland.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 16

events.title: The Wright brothers make the first sustained airplane flights
events.summary: Orville's first flight at Kill Devil Hills lasts 12 seconds.
events.description: On December 17, 1903, Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first successful sustained flights in an airplane at Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina. Orville went first, flying 120 feet in 12 seconds.
events.notificationTitle: Twelve seconds that changed travel
events.notificationBody: In 1903, the Wright brothers made the first sustained airplane flights.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 17

events.title: Queen Nzinga dies in Matamba
events.summary: The Mbundu ruler is remembered as the 'mother of the nation' in Angola.
events.description: On December 17, 1663, Nzinga, a Mbundu queen, died in Matamba. She is considered the 'mother of the nation' in Angola.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 17

events.title: NAFTA is signed
events.summary: Mexico, Canada, and the United States sign a free trade agreement.
events.description: On December 17, 1992, the leaders of Mexico, Canada, and the United States signed the North American Free Trade Agreement. It was replaced by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement in 2020.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 17

events.title: Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker premieres
events.summary: The ballet is first performed at the Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg.
events.description: On December 18, 1892, Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker was first presented at the Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg, Russia.
events.notificationTitle: The Nutcracker's first curtain
events.notificationBody: In 1892, Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker premiered in St. Petersburg.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: The Thirteenth Amendment abolishes slavery in the US
events.summary: The constitutional amendment officially enters into force.
events.description: On December 18, 1865, the Thirteenth Amendment to the US Constitution officially entered into force, abolishing slavery in the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: The Piltdown Man is announced
events.summary: A supposed 'missing link' fossil later proves to be a fraud.
events.description: On December 18, 1912, a British Museum paleontologist announced the discovery in England of fossil remains said to be an extinct human species. Presented as a missing link between apes and early humans, the Piltdown Man was exposed as a fraud by the 1950s.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: Antonio Stradivari dies in Cremona
events.summary: The famed Italian violin maker dies.
events.description: On December 18, 1737, the famed Italian violin maker Antonio Stradivari died in Cremona.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: Charles Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol
events.summary: Scrooge's story of redemption becomes an instant classic.
events.description: On December 19, 1843, Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol was published for the first time. Its story of Ebenezer Scrooge's redemption became an instant classic and is still retold on stage and screen.
events.notificationTitle: Bah, humbug, and a classic is born
events.notificationBody: In 1843, Charles Dickens published A Christmas Carol.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: Washington's army goes into winter quarters at Valley Forge
events.summary: About 11,000 Continental troops camp near British-occupied Philadelphia.
events.description: On December 19, 1777, during the American Revolution, General George Washington led 11,000 regulars into winter quarters at Valley Forge, on the Schuylkill River near British-occupied Philadelphia.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: Edith Piaf is born in Paris
events.summary: The singer who made the French chanson world famous is born.
events.description: On December 19, 1915, the singer and actress Edith Piaf, whose interpretation of the French chanson made her internationally famous, was born in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: South Korea elects its first woman president
events.summary: Park Geun-hye wins the presidential election.
events.description: On December 19, 2012, Park Geun-hye was elected the first female president of South Korea. She later became the country's first democratically elected president to be removed from office, after her impeachment in 2017.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: The Brothers Grimm publish their first volume of tales
events.summary: Stories like Hansel and Gretel and Snow White reach print.
events.description: On December 20, 1812, the brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm published the first volume of the stories that made them famous. Their collection, known as Grimm's Fairy Tales, includes 'Hansel and Gretel', 'Snow White', 'Little Red Riding Hood', and 'Sleeping Beauty'.
events.notificationTitle: Once upon a time, in print
events.notificationBody: In 1812, the Brothers Grimm published their first volume of fairy tales.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: Macau returns to Chinese sovereignty
events.summary: Centuries of Portuguese rule come to an end.
events.description: On December 20, 1999, centuries of Portuguese rule in Macau ended when it became a special administrative region under Chinese sovereignty, 12 years after China and Portugal agreed on its status.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: It's a Wonderful Life premieres
events.summary: Frank Capra's drama becomes a holiday classic.
events.description: On December 20, 1946, Frank Capra's It's a Wonderful Life, starring Jimmy Stewart, premiered. It later became a holiday classic.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: South Carolina secedes from the Union
events.summary: The first state to leave follows Lincoln's election.
events.description: On December 20, 1860, following Abraham Lincoln's election as president, South Carolina became the first US state to secede from the Union.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: The first game of basketball is played
events.summary: James Naismith's new game debuts in a Springfield school gym.
events.description: On December 21, 1891, the first game of basketball, organized by gym teacher James Naismith, was played at a school in Springfield, Massachusetts. The chaotic game prompted Naismith to develop the sport's original rules.
events.notificationTitle: Tip-off for a new sport
events.notificationBody: In 1891, the first game of basketball was played in Springfield.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

events.title: Apollo 8 launches toward the Moon
events.summary: The mission will complete ten lunar orbits.
events.description: On December 21, 1968, Apollo 8 was launched from Cape Kennedy and went on to complete 10 orbits of the Moon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

events.title: The first modern crossword puzzle is published
events.summary: The New York World introduces a new kind of word game.
events.description: On December 21, 1913, the New York World published the first modern crossword puzzle.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

events.title: The Brandenburg Gate reopens
events.summary: Berliners pass through the gate for the first time since 1961.
events.description: On December 22, 1989, the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin reopened as East and West Germany moved toward reunification. Berliners had been unable to use the gate since the Berlin Wall blocked it in 1961.
events.notificationTitle: Through the Brandenburg Gate again
events.notificationBody: In 1989, Berlin's Brandenburg Gate reopened after 28 years.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: Srinivasa Ramanujan is born
events.summary: The self-taught Indian mathematician is born in Erode.
events.description: On December 22, 1887, Srinivasa Ramanujan, a self-taught Indian mathematician who made many pioneering discoveries, was born in Erode in present-day Tamil Nadu.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: The pope sanctions the Dominican order
events.summary: Honorius III approves the Order of Preachers.
events.description: On December 22, 1216, the Dominican order was sanctioned by Pope Honorius III.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: Leo the Deacon records the solar corona during an eclipse
events.summary: Leo the Deacon's account is the earliest datable description of the corona.
events.description: On December 22, 968, an eclipse of the Sun occurred, and Leo the Deacon described a feeble glow, like a narrow headband, around the darkened Sun: the earliest account of the solar corona that can be linked to a datable eclipse.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: George Washington resigns as commander in chief
events.summary: The victorious general returns his commission to Congress.
events.description: On December 23, 1783, before the Continental Congress, George Washington resigned as commander in chief of the Continental Army.
events.notificationTitle: The general who gave back his power
events.notificationBody: In 1783, George Washington resigned as commander in chief.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: The Ottoman Empire's first constitution takes effect
events.summary: The document gives the sultan full executive power.
events.description: On December 23, 1876, the first comprehensive constitution of the Ottoman Empire went into effect, giving the sultan full executive power.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: The Federal Reserve System is created
events.summary: President Wilson signs the Federal Reserve Act.
events.description: On December 23, 1913, President Woodrow Wilson signed the Federal Reserve Act, bringing the Federal Reserve System into being.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: Jean-Francois Champollion is born
events.summary: The French linguist and historian is born.
events.description: On December 23, 1790, the French historian and linguist Jean-Francois Champollion was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: Edison applies to patent the phonograph
events.summary: The 'speaking machine' is filed with the US Patent Office.
events.description: On December 24, 1877, the US Patent Office received Thomas Edison's application for a 'Phonograph or Speaking Machine'. He had first demonstrated the device weeks earlier by playing back his recorded voice.
events.notificationTitle: A machine that talks back
events.notificationBody: In 1877, Thomas Edison applied to patent the phonograph.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

events.title: The Treaty of Ghent ends the War of 1812
events.summary: The United States and Britain make peace in Belgium.
events.description: On December 24, 1814, the United States and Great Britain signed the Treaty of Ghent in Belgium, ending the War of 1812.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

events.title: Libya becomes independent under King Idris I
events.summary: The new North African kingdom crowns its first monarch.
events.description: On December 24, 1951, Idris I became the first king of newly independent Libya.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

events.title: The James Webb Space Telescope launches
events.summary: Hubble's successor lifts off on Christmas Day.
events.description: On December 25, 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope, designed and built by US, Canadian, and European space agencies as the successor to the Hubble Space Telescope, was launched into space.
events.notificationTitle: A Christmas gift to astronomy
events.notificationBody: On Christmas Day 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope launched.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
events.summary: The king of the Franks becomes the first emperor of the Holy Roman Empire.
events.description: On December 25, 800, Charlemagne, king of the Franks, became the first emperor of what became the Holy Roman Empire.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: William the Conqueror is crowned king of England
events.summary: The coronation completes the Norman Conquest.
events.description: On December 25, 1066, William I was crowned king of England, formally completing the Norman Conquest.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Washington crosses the Delaware
events.summary: A Christmas night crossing leads to a surprise attack at Trenton.
events.description: On December 25, 1776, during the American Revolution, General George Washington crossed the Delaware River and surprised the British at Trenton, New Jersey.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president
events.summary: The Soviet Union ceases to exist at the end of the year.
events.description: On December 25, 1991, Mikhail Gorbachev resigned the presidency of the Soviet Union, which ceased to exist at the end of the year.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25
